Let $D$ be a finite ordered quantum register and let $A$ be an ordered register of $k\ge0$ ancilla qubits, with Hilbert spaces $\mathcal H_D$ and $\mathcal H_A$. Write $|0_A\rangle=|0^k\rangle$, including $|0_A\rangle=1$ when $k=0$. Let $U$ be a unitary on $\mathcal H_D\otimes\mathcal H_A$ and let $V$ be a unitary on $\mathcal H_D$.

The register $A$ is a **clean ancilla register for $U$ and $V$** when
$$
U(|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|0_A\rangle
$$
for every vector $|\psi\rangle_D$. Thus the data operation is independent of the input vector and all clean wires return exactly to zero.

The register $A$ is a **dirty ancilla register for $U$ and $V$** when the operator identity $U=V\otimes I_A$ holds on $\mathcal H_D\otimes\mathcal H_A$. Equivalently, every product input $|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|\eta\rangle_A$ is mapped to $V|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|\eta\rangle_A$, with the same $V$ for every data and ancilla vector. This requires exact restoration of an arbitrary, initially unknown ancilla state and forbids residual data–ancilla correlation.

These are exact contracts for the complete subroutine. A temporary intermediate alteration of an ancilla is permitted if the full unitary satisfies the stated identity.

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered list of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces with specified ordered orthonormal bases of
sizes $d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1}$, allowing $d_k=0$. The elementary tensors of the
factor bases, ordered lexicographically, form an orthonormal basis of the
tensor register, and

$$\dim(H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1})=\prod_{k<n}d_k.$$

For the empty list the product is $1$ and the tensor space is $\mathbb C$; if
any $d_k=0$, the tensor space is zero and the product basis is empty.

For any linear map $A$ with adjoint and vectors $u,v$, conjugate symmetry and the defining adjoint relation give $\langle A^\dagger q,v\rangle_{\rm root}=\overline{\langle v,A^\dagger q\rangle_{\rm root}}=\overline{\langle Av,q\rangle_{\rm root}}=\langle q,Av\rangle_{\rm root}$ for every $q$. Hence $A R_{u,v}A^\dagger=R_{Au,Av}$. By [F3], $R_{w,z}\otimes P_0=R_{w\otimes|0_A\rangle,z\otimes|0_A\rangle}$. Apply the rank-one identity with $A=I_R\otimes U$, $u=e_i\otimes|0_A\rangle$, and $v=e_j\otimes|0_A\rangle$, where $e_i,e_j$ range over the product orthonormal basis of $R\otimes D$. Step 1.1 gives the clean conjugation formula for each $R_{e_i,e_j}\otimes P_0$. Every matrix $X$ on $R\otimes D$ equals $\sum_{i,j}\langle Xe_j,e_i\rangle_{\rm root}R_{e_i,e_j}$, since the right side agrees with $X$ on each basis vector; hence these matrix units span and linearity proves the clean identity for every $X$.

In the dirty case, [F1] and [F2] give $I_R\otimes U=I_R\otimes V\otimes I_A$ on every elementary tensor and hence on the whole product space. derivations.claim: The matrix in [F5] sends $|t\rangle$ to $|t\oplus1\rangle$. Applying it twice sends $t$ to $t\oplus1\oplus1=t$, so $X^2=I$.
By [F1], applying CNOT twice sends $|a,t\rangle$ to $|a,t\oplus a\oplus a\rangle=|a,t\rangle$, so $\operatorname{CNOT}^2=I$.
Applying $T$ twice leaves $a,b$ unchanged and sends $t$ to $t\oplus ab\oplus ab=t$. Thus $T^2=I$.

When the Fredkin control is $0$, each application fixes $(a,b)$. When it is $1$, each application swaps $a,b$ and leaves the control unchanged. In either case two applications restore all three bits, so $F^2=I$.

The four maps permute the ordered orthonormal computational basis by [F1]–[F5]. A permutation of an orthonormal basis preserves inner products, so each linear extension is unitary; by Steps 1.1–1.4 each is its own inverse.

Apply the gates chronologically as prescribed by [F6] to $|c,a,b\rangle$. After CNOT$(a,b)$ the last two bits are $(a,b\oplus a)$. If $c=0$, Toffoli does nothing and the last CNOT restores $(a,b)$. If $c=1$, Toffoli changes its target to $a\oplus(b\oplus a)=b$, and the last CNOT changes the other bit to $(b\oplus a)\oplus b=a$. Thus the output is $|c,a,b\rangle$ for $c=0$ and $|c,b,a\rangle$ for $c=1$, exactly the Fredkin action.

A Boolean circuit on $n$ inputs is a finite directed acyclic graph with inputs
$x_1,\ldots,x_n$, constants $0$ and $1$, and NOT, AND, and OR gates; AND and
OR have fan-in two, while NOT has fan-in one. One node is designated as the
**output**. The circuit's value is the value at that node after evaluating the
graph in topological order. Its **size** is its number of non-input gates, and
its **depth** is the largest number of non-input gates on a directed path
ending at the output (a path may begin at an input or a constant).

If two fixed finite bounded-arity bases can simulate every gate (and every
constant) of one another by fixed finite circuits, then changing between them
costs only constant factors in size and depth. In particular this holds for
any two such functionally complete bases with simulable constants. No such
claim is made for an arbitrary finite basis that may fail to express one of
the Boolean operations.

Inputs are integers $n,m\ge0$, $n$ distinct ordered Boolean input wires, an $m$-bit target register $y$ disjoint from the input wires, and a finite Boolean DAG with an explicit topological order and an ordered list of exactly $m$ output ports. Every vertex has a unique identifier; each non-input node is a constant $0$ or $1$, a NOT node of fan-in one, or an AND or OR node of fan-in two. Each source reference must name an input vertex or an earlier node in the supplied order. Each output port may name any input or non-input node, and repeated output ports are allowed. The Boolean graph uses the NOT/AND/OR basis with constants from [[def-boolean-circuit-size-depth-fanin-and-basis]], extended here to multiple ordered output ports sharing one graph.

Return INVALID if the input wires or graph vertices do not have distinct identifiers, a target wire overlaps an input or graph vertex, an unsupported gate or incorrect fan-in occurs, a source reference is unavailable at that position, the supplied order is invalid, or an output port names no available vertex. Otherwise:

1. Allocate one fresh clean value bit $w_v$ for each non-input node $v$.
2. Process nodes in the supplied order. Leave a constant-$0$ bit untouched; apply $X$ to a constant-$1$ bit. For a NOT node with input wire $u$, apply $X(w_v)$ then $\operatorname{CNOT}_{u\to w_v}$. For an AND node with inputs $u,v$, apply $T(u,v,w_v)$. For an OR node, apply $\operatorname{CNOT}_{u\to w_v}$, then $\operatorname{CNOT}_{v\to w_v}$, then $T(u,v,w_v)$. If a two-port node uses the same source identifier twice, first allocate a fresh clean scratch bit $s$, copy the source into $s$ by CNOT, use the distinct physical wires as the gate inputs, and uncopy $s$ immediately after writing $w_v$.
3. For each output port $j$, apply CNOT from its named input or value wire to target bit $y_j$.
4. Append the inverse of the entire node-evaluation list in reverse chronological order, including the temporary source-copy and uncopy instructions. Return the resulting finite gate list, with the input register unchanged and the target changed only by the stated XOR into $y$.

The inverse-list operation is defined instruction by instruction: $X$, CNOT, and Toffoli are each replaced by themselves, in reverse order. The Boolean graph is an explicit finite input; this procedure makes no uniform-generation, oracle, or Turing-time claim.

Let $a,b$ be distinct source wires and let $t$ be a distinct target wire initialized to $0$. The chronological sequence $X(t)$ followed by $\operatorname{CNOT}_{a\to t}$ writes $1\oplus a$ into $t$. The sequence $\operatorname{CNOT}_{a\to t}$, $\operatorname{CNOT}_{b\to t}$, $T(a,b,t)$ writes $a\lor b$ into $t$, since $a\lor b=a\oplus b\oplus ab$. Every source wire is unchanged.

Let $a,b$ be the values on two distinct control wires, let $t$ be a distinct clean target wire with value $0$, and let $y$ be another distinct target wire with arbitrary value. Toffoli changes $t$ to $ab$ while preserving the controls. Copying that value into $y$ by CNOT and applying Toffoli again, in the written chronological order, sends
$$
|a,b,y,0\rangle\longmapsto|a,b,y\oplus ab,0\rangle.
$$
The same operator identity holds on superpositions.

Let $U$ and $V$ satisfy either the clean or dirty identity in [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]], and let $R$ be any finite ordered reference register. Put $P_0=R_{0_A,0_A}$, where the rank-one operator notation used here is defined by $R_{u,v}(z)=\langle z,v\rangle_{\rm root}u$. In the clean case, for every matrix $X$ on $R\otimes D$,
$$
(I_R\otimes U)(X\otimes P_0)(I_R\otimes U^\dagger)=\big((I_R\otimes V)X(I_R\otimes V^\dagger)\big)\otimes P_0.
$$
In the dirty case, for every matrix $Y$ on $R\otimes D\otimes A$,
$$
(I_R\otimes U)Y(I_R\otimes U^\dagger)=(I_R\otimes V\otimes I_A)Y(I_R\otimes V^\dagger\otimes I_A).
$$
Thus the stated identities apply in particular to density matrices, meaning positive semidefinite matrices of trace one.

On the ordered computational basis, $X$, CNOT, Toffoli $T$, and Fredkin $F$ are involutions. Their linear extensions are unitary. With chronological order meaning the gates are applied in the written order, Fredkin is implemented by CNOT$(a,b)$, then $T(c,b,a)$, then CNOT$(a,b)$.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

For $n\ge0$ and a binary word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})\in\{0,1\}^n$, define its
**big-endian index**

$$\operatorname{enc}_n(x):=\sum_{k<n}x_k\,2^{\,n-1-k}.$$

Thus the first wire is the most significant bit. For $n=0$, the domain
$\{0,1\}^0$ consists only of the empty word $()$, and the empty sum gives
$\operatorname{enc}_0(())=0$. In an ordered $n$-qubit
computational basis, the word $x$ occupies the slot numbered
$\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$.

For every $n\ge0$, the map
$\operatorname{enc}_n:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,\ldots,2^n-1\}$ of
[[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]] is a bijection. Any permutation of the
$n$ bit positions therefore induces a permutation of the corresponding
computational basis.

For a gate occurrence $g=(\gamma,w)$ in a circuit on $\mathcal Q_n$, let $\widetilde U_g$ be the global embedding from [[lem-qc-local-gate-wire-embedding]]. For a layer $L_t=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$, define
$$U_{L_t}:=\widetilde U_{g_s}\cdots\widetilde U_{g_1}.$$
For a circuit with chronological layers $L_1,\ldots,L_d$, define
$$U_C:=U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}.$$
The empty circuit and every empty layer denote the identity on $\mathcal Q_n$.

Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered list of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces with specified ordered orthonormal bases of
sizes $d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1}$, allowing $d_k=0$. The elementary tensors of the
factor bases, ordered lexicographically, form an orthonormal basis of the
tensor register, and

$$\dim(H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1})=\prod_{k<n}d_k.$$

For the empty list the product is $1$ and the tensor space is $\mathbb C$; if
any $d_k=0$, the tensor space is zero and the product basis is empty.

Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$ with maximum arity $k:=\max(\{r(g):g\in G\}\cup\{0\})$ and a circuit from [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The declared **size** is the number of gate occurrences, equivalently $\sum_{t=1}^d|L_t|$; the declared **depth** is the number $d$ of explicit layers, not a minimum over alternate layerings; the **width** is the number $n$ of all wires, including workspace wires. The operation model may also assign weighted gate costs, classical bit costs, and query costs; these are separate coordinates and are summed over the calls actually made.

A workspace wire is an ancilla. A **clean-ancilla promise** specifies computational-basis zero states for the ancillas and requires their exact return for every allowed data input: if $U$ is the implemented unitary, $V_D$ is the declared data unitary, and $|0_A\rangle$ is the specified joint zero vector, then $U(x\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V_Dx\otimes|0_A\rangle$ for every allowed data vector $x$. A **dirty-ancilla promise** permits an arbitrary ancilla state independent of the data input; it may be correlated with an untouched reference. Exact dirty-ancilla restoration means the implemented unitary on data and ancillas is $V_D\otimes I_A$ on the entire joint space, where $V_D$ is the declared unitary on data. The same operator equality then holds after tensoring with the identity on any finite untouched reference. Consequently, product input between the data and the combined ancilla/reference system remains product after the operation. No uncorrelated-output claim is made for an initially data-correlated ancilla.

A controlled or inverse operation is counted only when the operation model explicitly grants that access or supplies a construction; its charge is recorded separately from an ordinary call. Inverse availability and query or gate charges are also recorded separately from controlled forward access. In particular, the matrix of $U$ alone supplies neither a controlled call nor an inverse query, in accordance with [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]].

derivations.claim: Let $q$ be the number of two-port nodes whose two ports name the same source. Each non-input node uses at most three evaluation gates: at most one for a constant, two for NOT, one for AND, and three for OR. Each repeated-source node adds one CNOT copy and one uncopy, so the forward pass uses at most $3S+2q$ gates. Since each such node accounts for two of the $E$ port uses, $q\le E$, and the forward bound is at most $3S+2E$. It uses $S$ value bits and $q\le E$ temporary bits.

The $m$ output ports are copied by $m$ CNOTs into distinct target bits. Reversing the complete node-evaluation list uses at most another $3S+2E$ gates. By [F6], each gate is its own inverse; reversing both order and gate sequence therefore implements the inverse computation and returns every value and temporary bit to zero. The total is at most $2(3S+2E)+m=6S+4E+m$ gate occurrences. A serial execution assigns each occurrence its own explicit layer, so the depth has the same bound by [F13]; [F11] specifies the chronological operator product.

Use [F9]–[F10] to identify each ordered bit string with its unique basis vector. Induct along the supplied topological order. A constant-$0$ node leaves its zero bit unchanged and a constant-$1$ node uses [F8]; NOT and OR nodes receive the outputs in [F3], and AND nodes receive the output in [F4]. If a two-port node repeats a source value $c$, its fresh scratch bit is set to $c$ by CNOT; the two distinct physical control wires then both hold $c$, so AND gives $c\land c=c$ and OR gives $c\lor c=c$. The scratch is immediately uncomputed by the same CNOT. Thus every value bit equals its Boolean node value and all temporary bits are zero before the output copy. The $m$ output CNOTs produce $y\oplus f(x)$; reversing the node list then restores every work bit without touching the input or target registers, whose order is fixed by [F7]. Since applying $y\mapsto y\oplus f(x)$ twice returns $y$, the target action is a permutation of the ordered basis and is unitary by [F12]; the compiled gate list is unitary by [F6] and [F11].

The basis identity in Step 3.1 extends by linearity to every input vector, so it is the clean-ancilla identity required by [F5]. The lemma then extends it to every finite reference register and every matrix, hence to density matrices. The construction uses only the supplied finite list; no choice principle is used.

derivations.claim: Apply $O_f$ twice to a basis vector. The first application gives $|x,y\oplus f(x)\rangle$; the second gives $|x,(y\oplus f(x))\oplus f(x)\rangle=|x,y\rangle$ because every bit added modulo two twice is zero. The input $x$ is preserved throughout, so injectivity of $f$ is not needed.

By [F2]–[F6], the input and target strings label the entire finite orthonormal product basis in the declared order. Step 1.1 shows that the oracle map is a permutation of this basis, so its matrix has orthonormal columns and satisfies $O_f^\dagger O_f=I$. Therefore it is unitary, and Step 1.1 gives its inverse as itself.

$$H:=\frac{X+Z}{\sqrt2}=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad S:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&i\end{pmatrix},\qquad T:=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&e^{i\pi/4}\end{pmatrix}.$$

For real $\theta$ and a real unit vector $\mathbf n=(n_x,n_y,n_z)$, define the axis rotation
$$R_{\mathbf n}(\theta):=\exp\!\left(-\frac{i\theta}{2}\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}\right),\qquad R_z(\theta):=R_{(0,0,1)}(\theta).$$
Here $\mathbf n\cdot\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ and $\|\mathbf n\|_2$ have the meanings fixed in [[def-qc-bloch-coordinate-map]]. Let $n,m\ge0$, $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, and $y\in\{0,1\}^m$. Let a finite topologically ordered Boolean DAG have $S$ non-input nodes, including constants, and $E$ input-port uses counted with multiplicity. Its gates are NOT, AND, OR, and constants, with fan-in at most two, and it has $m$ ordered output ports computing $f(x)$. Under the fixed elementary alphabet in [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]], counting each occurrence of $X$, CNOT, and Toffoli as one gate and one serial layer, [[alg-qc-reversible-embedding]] returns a circuit on the ordered input, target, and work registers implementing
$$
|x,y,0^w\rangle\longmapsto|x,y\oplus f(x),0^w\rangle
$$
for every basis input $x$ and every target string $y$. It uses at most $6S+4E+m$ elementary gate occurrences, at most $S+E$ clean work bits, and serial depth at most $6S+4E+m$. The same operator action holds coherently on arbitrary superpositions and after adjoining any finite reference register.

Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$ with maximum arity $k:=\max(\{r(g):g\in G\}\cup\{0\})$ and a circuit from [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The declared **size** is the number of gate occurrences, equivalently $\sum_{t=1}^d|L_t|$; the declared **depth** is the number $d$ of explicit layers, not a minimum over alternate layerings; the **width** is the number $n$ of all wires, including workspace wires. The operation model may also assign weighted gate costs, classical bit costs, and query costs; these are separate coordinates and are summed over the calls actually made.

A workspace wire is an ancilla. A **clean-ancilla promise** specifies computational-basis zero states for the ancillas and requires their exact return for every allowed data input: if $U$ is the implemented unitary, $V_D$ is the declared data unitary, and $|0_A\rangle$ is the specified joint zero vector, then $U(x\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V_Dx\otimes|0_A\rangle$ for every allowed data vector $x$. A **dirty-ancilla promise** permits an arbitrary ancilla state independent of the data input; it may be correlated with an untouched reference. Exact dirty-ancilla restoration means the implemented unitary on data and ancillas is $V_D\otimes I_A$ on the entire joint space, where $V_D$ is the declared unitary on data. The same operator equality then holds after tensoring with the identity on any finite untouched reference. Consequently, product input between the data and the combined ancilla/reference system remains product after the operation. No uncorrelated-output claim is made for an initially data-correlated ancilla.

A controlled or inverse operation is counted only when the operation model explicitly grants that access or supplies a construction; its charge is recorded separately from an ordinary call. Inverse availability and query or gate charges are also recorded separately from controlled forward access. In particular, the matrix of $U$ alone supplies neither a controlled call nor an inverse query, in accordance with [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]].

For a gate occurrence $g=(\gamma,w)$ in a circuit on $\mathcal Q_n$, let $\widetilde U_g$ be the global embedding from [[lem-qc-local-gate-wire-embedding]]. For a layer $L_t=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$, define
$$U_{L_t}:=\widetilde U_{g_s}\cdots\widetilde U_{g_1}.$$
For a circuit with chronological layers $L_1,\ldots,L_d$, define
$$U_C:=U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}.$$
The empty circuit and every empty layer denote the identity on $\mathcal Q_n$.

An **ordered tensor register** consists of a finite ordered list of
finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$, each
equipped with a specified ordered orthonormal basis. Its space is
$H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}$, with factors retained in the displayed
order. The product basis is ordered lexicographically by its tuple of factor
indices. The empty tensor product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. A
zero-dimensional factor is allowed in this mathematical construction and makes
the tensor space zero; it is not a register under
[[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]].

The inner product is linear in the first argument and conjugate-linear in the
second, and on elementary tensors it is

$$\left\langle\bigotimes_{k<n}x_k,\bigotimes_{k<n}y_k\right\rangle_{\otimes}:=\prod_{k<n}\langle x_k,y_k\rangle_{{\rm root},k}.$$ 

For the empty tensor, the right side is the empty product $1$, giving the
standard inner product on $\mathbb C$.

For a permutation $\sigma$ of the $n$ factor positions, the **wire permutation**
$P_\sigma$ maps the product basis vector indexed by
$(i_0,\ldots,i_{n-1})$ to the product basis vector whose output factor order is
$(\sigma(0),\ldots,\sigma(n-1))$. It is extended linearly; for $n=0$ it is the
identity on $\mathbb C$. The extension is a linear map in the sense of
[[def-linear-map]].

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

In the ordered two-qubit basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$, the controlled-NOT with first wire control and second wire target is

$$\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}|a,t\rangle=|a,t\mathbin{\oplus}a\rangle,\qquad a,t\in\{0,1\}.$$

Equivalently, it is the control block $C(X)=\operatorname{diag}(I,X)$ of [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]], where $X$ is the Pauli bit-flip matrix. The wire order is part of the definition.

In the ordered computational basis $(|0\rangle,|1\rangle)$ of [[def-qc-qubit-and-bloch-representation]], define the identity and Pauli endomorphisms of $Q_2$ by
$$I=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix},\qquad X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\qquad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}.$$

The displayed sign in $Y$ fixes all later orientation and rotation conventions.

All bits are in $\mathbb F_2=\{0,1\}$, with addition denoted by $\oplus$ and multiplication by juxtaposition. On three distinct ordered computational-basis wires, define the Toffoli gate $T$ and Fredkin gate $F$ by
$$
T|a,b,t\rangle=|a,b,t\oplus ab\rangle,
$$
and
$$
F|0,a,b\rangle=|0,a,b\rangle,\qquad F|1,a,b\rangle=|1,b,a\rangle.
$$
These basis actions extend linearly. Wire order is exactly the order displayed; the first two wires of $T$ are controls and the third is its target, while the first wire of $F$ is its control and the other two are conditionally swapped. Negative-control variants mean conjugating the chosen positive control by $X$ before and after the gate. These are fixed arity-three labels in the declared finite gate alphabet, not implicit access to arbitrary multicontrol gates. Their reversibility is established in [[lem-qc-x-cnot-toffoli-and-fredkin-are-involutions]].

Let $a,b$ be distinct source wires and let $t$ be a distinct target wire initialized to $0$. The chronological sequence $X(t)$ followed by $\operatorname{CNOT}_{a\to t}$ writes $1\oplus a$ into $t$. The sequence $\operatorname{CNOT}_{a\to t}$, $\operatorname{CNOT}_{b\to t}$, $T(a,b,t)$ writes $a\lor b$ into $t$, since $a\lor b=a\oplus b\oplus ab$. Every source wire is unchanged.

On the ordered computational basis, $X$, CNOT, Toffoli $T$, and Fredkin $F$ are involutions. Their linear extensions are unitary. With chronological order meaning the gates are applied in the written order, Fredkin is implemented by CNOT$(a,b)$, then $T(c,b,a)$, then CNOT$(a,b)$.

For every $d\ge1$, the ordered computational basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of
the register $Q_d$ from [[def-qc-register-and-computational-basis]] is an
orthonormal basis for its declared inner product. Separately, the one-dimensional
zero-qubit register has the basis $\{1\}$ by definition.

Let $H_0,\ldots,H_{n-1}$ be a finite ordered list of finite-dimensional
complex inner-product spaces with specified ordered orthonormal bases of
sizes $d_0,\ldots,d_{n-1}$, allowing $d_k=0$. The elementary tensors of the
factor bases, ordered lexicographically, form an orthonormal basis of the
tensor register, and

$$\dim(H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1})=\prod_{k<n}d_k.$$

For the empty list the product is $1$ and the tensor space is $\mathbb C$; if
any $d_k=0$, the tensor space is zero and the product basis is empty.

For $n\ge0$ and a binary word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})\in\{0,1\}^n$, define its
**big-endian index**

$$\operatorname{enc}_n(x):=\sum_{k<n}x_k\,2^{\,n-1-k}.$$

Thus the first wire is the most significant bit. For $n=0$, the domain
$\{0,1\}^0$ consists only of the empty word $()$, and the empty sum gives
$\operatorname{enc}_0(())=0$. In an ordered $n$-qubit
computational basis, the word $x$ occupies the slot numbered
$\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$.

For every $n\ge0$, the map
$\operatorname{enc}_n:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,\ldots,2^n-1\}$ of
[[def-qc-ordered-bitstring-encoding]] is a bijection. Any permutation of the
$n$ bit positions therefore induces a permutation of the corresponding
computational basis.

derivations.claim: For a source wire used $r\ge1$ times in one DAG layer, start with that wire as one leaf and in each round apply CNOT from each current leaf to at most one fresh zero target. After $j$ rounds there are at least $\min(r,2^j)$ distinct leaves, so at most $\lceil\log_2(r+1)\rceil\le L$ rounds suffice. The tree needs $r-1$ CNOTs, and summing $r-1$ over source wires and layers gives at most $E$ copies. By [F4], each leaf carries the source's basis value and each CNOT leaves its control unchanged. The rounds are successive explicit layers in the order specified by [F9], counted by [F10].

Fix a DAG layer and suppose each source wire at its start holds its Boolean circuit value. Fan out every source to private leaves by Step 1.1. Each non-input node has a distinct fresh zero value bit. A constant-$0$ node leaves that bit unchanged, and a constant-$1$ node flips it by [F5]. For NOT, the two sublayers in [F7] write $1\oplus a$; for AND, [F6] writes $ab$; for OR, [F7] writes $a\oplus b\oplus ab=a\lor b$. Repeated logical sources have distinct physical leaves, and every gate preserves its leaves. Targets are distinct between nodes, so each of these at most three gate sublayers has disjoint supports. Reversing the fan-out trees restores all private leaves to zero, since the evaluation gates did not change them; [F8] supplies the inverse CNOTs. By [F9] these are chronological sublayers, and [F10] counts them. The layer therefore takes at most $L+3+L=2L+3$ depth.

If a non-input node $u$ feeds a node $v$, every longest path ending at $u$ extends by that edge, so the layer index of $u$ is strictly smaller than the layer index of $v$. Induct on the layer index. At the first layer all non-input predecessors are absent; at a later layer every non-input predecessor has its correct value by induction. Step 2.1 then writes the Boolean value of each node in the current layer and clears its temporary leaves. Thus after all $D$ layers every value bit equals its node's Boolean evaluation, including when two ports use the same source, and all fan-out leaves are zero.

For each output source selected $r$ times, use Step 1.1 to produce $r$ private leaves in at most $L_m$ rounds. Copy each leaf into its distinct target bit in one layer, then reverse the tree in at most $L_m$ rounds. Summing $r-1$ over output sources gives at most $m$ temporary targets, and the output stage has depth at most $2L_m+1$. This also covers repeated output ports and output sources that are input wires. The chronological composition is the one in [F9], and [F10] counts the explicit layers.

Copy each output into its target, then reverse the layer computations. In reverse order the fan-out tree is first recreated, the node gates are inverted to clear their value bits, and the fan-out tree is then undone; [F8] makes these same CNOT, X, and Toffoli gates available as inverses. This costs at most another $D(2L+3)$ depth and returns every value bit and temporary copy to zero. Adding this reverse depth, the output stage from Step 4.1, and the forward depth from Steps 2.1–3.1 gives $2D(2L+3)+2L_m+1$. There are $S$ value bits, at most $E$ temporary input-copy bits, and at most $m$ output-copy bits, for $O(S+E+m)$ work. The input-copy trees and their reversals in both computation passes use at most $4E$ CNOTs, and the output-copy trees and their reversals use at most $2m$ CNOTs, output copying uses $m$ CNOTs, and Boolean evaluation and reversal use at most $6S$ gates, hence the total is $O(S+E+m)$. Since fan-in is at most two, $E\le2S$. By Step 3.1 each output source holds its Boolean value, so Step 4.1 changes the target to $y\oplus f(x)$; reversing node computations restores the work without changing the input or target. This is the XOR embedding specified by [F1]. By [F11]–[F14], ordered bit strings identify the complete computational basis of the input, target, and work registers, including the zero-qubit case; the basis identity therefore extends by linearity to superpositions. The finite circuit denotes the chronological operator product [F9], its resource coordinates are counted by [F10], and fan-out CNOTs may entangle copies during computation, but reversing them restores each copy bit to zero, so no arbitrary unknown state is cloned.

Let $D$ be a finite ordered quantum register and let $A$ be an ordered register of $k\ge0$ ancilla qubits, with Hilbert spaces $\mathcal H_D$ and $\mathcal H_A$. Write $|0_A\rangle=|0^k\rangle$, including $|0_A\rangle=1$ when $k=0$. Let $U$ be a unitary on $\mathcal H_D\otimes\mathcal H_A$ and let $V$ be a unitary on $\mathcal H_D$.

The register $A$ is a **clean ancilla register for $U$ and $V$** when
$$
U(|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|0_A\rangle
$$
for every vector $|\psi\rangle_D$. Thus the data operation is independent of the input vector and all clean wires return exactly to zero.

The register $A$ is a **dirty ancilla register for $U$ and $V$** when the operator identity $U=V\otimes I_A$ holds on $\mathcal H_D\otimes\mathcal H_A$. Equivalently, every product input $|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|\eta\rangle_A$ is mapped to $V|\psi\rangle_D\otimes|\eta\rangle_A$, with the same $V$ for every data and ancilla vector. This requires exact restoration of an arbitrary, initially unknown ancilla state and forbids residual data–ancilla correlation.

These are exact contracts for the complete subroutine. A temporary intermediate alteration of an ancilla is permitted if the full unitary satisfies the stated identity.

Let $U$ and $V$ satisfy either the clean or dirty identity in [[def-qc-clean-and-dirty-ancillas]], and let $R$ be any finite ordered reference register. Put $P_0=R_{0_A,0_A}$, where the rank-one operator notation used here is defined by $R_{u,v}(z)=\langle z,v\rangle_{\rm root}u$. In the clean case, for every matrix $X$ on $R\otimes D$,
$$
(I_R\otimes U)(X\otimes P_0)(I_R\otimes U^\dagger)=\big((I_R\otimes V)X(I_R\otimes V^\dagger)\big)\otimes P_0.
$$
In the dirty case, for every matrix $Y$ on $R\otimes D\otimes A$,
$$
(I_R\otimes U)Y(I_R\otimes U^\dagger)=(I_R\otimes V\otimes I_A)Y(I_R\otimes V^\dagger\otimes I_A).
$$
Thus the stated identities apply in particular to density matrices, meaning positive semidefinite matrices of trace one.

In the ordered two-qubit basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$, the controlled-NOT with first wire control and second wire target is

$$\operatorname{CNOT}_{1\to2}|a,t\rangle=|a,t\mathbin{\oplus}a\rangle,\qquad a,t\in\{0,1\}.$$

Equivalently, it is the control block $C(X)=\operatorname{diag}(I,X)$ of [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]], where $X$ is the Pauli bit-flip matrix. The wire order is part of the definition.

For a finite ordered family of finite-dimensional complex vector spaces
$H_k,K_k$ and complex-linear maps $T_k:H_k\to K_k$, the **tensor map**
$\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k:H_0\otimes\cdots\otimes H_{n-1}\to
K_0\otimes\cdots\otimes K_{n-1}$ is the unique linear map satisfying

$$\left(\bigotimes_{k<n}T_k\right)(x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes x_{n-1})=T_0x_0\otimes\cdots\otimes T_{n-1}x_{n-1}.$$

For $n=0$, the tensor map is the identity map $z\mapsto z$ on the empty tensor
product $\mathbb C$.

For a gate occurrence $g=(\gamma,w)$ in a circuit on $\mathcal Q_n$, let $\widetilde U_g$ be the global embedding from [[lem-qc-local-gate-wire-embedding]]. For a layer $L_t=(g_1,\ldots,g_s)$, define
$$U_{L_t}:=\widetilde U_{g_s}\cdots\widetilde U_{g_1}.$$
For a circuit with chronological layers $L_1,\ldots,L_d$, define
$$U_C:=U_{L_d}\cdots U_{L_1}.$$
The empty circuit and every empty layer denote the identity on $\mathcal Q_n$.

Let $C$ be a finite measurement-free unitary circuit. Assume that for every gate occurrence its adjoint is a legal gate occurrence on the same ordered wires and that the operation model explicitly grants each inverse call, as required by [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]]. Reverse the chronological layer order and, within each layer, reverse its gate list while replacing each gate by its adjoint. The resulting circuit $C^{-1}$ has
$$U_{C^{-1}}=U_C^\dagger=U_C^{-1}.$$
It has the same number of gate occurrences as $C$; inverse calls retain their separately declared access cost.

For an integer $d\ge 1$, the $d$-level register is the complex inner-product
space $Q_d=\mathbb C^d$ with the standard pairing
$\langle z,w\rangle_{\rm root}=\sum_{j<d}z_j\overline{w_j}$, linear in the
first argument as in [[def-real-and-complex-inner-product-space]] and
[[prop-standard-coordinate-inner-products]]. Its **computational basis** is the
ordered standard basis $(e_0,\ldots,e_{d-1})$ of [[lem-standard-basis-of-f-n]].
The register's alphabet is the ordered set $\{0,\ldots,d-1\}$.

For $n\ge0$, the $n$-qubit register is the ordered tensor product over
$\mathbb C$ of $n$ copies of $Q_2$. Here $\otimes_{\mathbb C}$ is the algebraic
module tensor product ([[def-tensor-product-of-modules-by-generators-and-relations]]),
with its complex-module structure and finite iterated/empty-product conventions
from [[thm-commutative-ring-module-structure-on-a-tensor-product]] and
[[cor-finite-iterated-tensor-products-represent-multilinear-maps]]. The tuple of
bit positions is ordered lexicographically, with the first wire as the most
significant position; the product-basis theorem below establishes the
corresponding elementary tensors as a basis. For $n=0$, the empty tensor
product is $\mathbb C$ with basis $\{1\}$. This one-dimensional trivial
register is distinct from the zero vector space $\mathbb C^0$. By definition a
register has positive dimension; a zero-dimensional space may still occur as a
factor in the more general tensor-space construction below.

For $n\ge0$ and a binary word $x=(x_0,\ldots,x_{n-1})\in\{0,1\}^n$, define its
**big-endian index**

$$\operatorname{enc}_n(x):=\sum_{k<n}x_k\,2^{\,n-1-k}.$$

Thus the first wire is the most significant bit. For $n=0$, the domain
$\{0,1\}^0$ consists only of the empty word $()$, and the empty sum gives
$\operatorname{enc}_0(())=0$. In an ordered $n$-qubit
computational basis, the word $x$ occupies the slot numbered
$\operatorname{enc}_n(x)$.

Let $n,m\ge0$ and let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^m$ be a total Boolean function on ordered bit strings. Its coherent XOR oracle is the linear extension of
$$
O_f|x,y\rangle=|x,y\oplus f(x)\rangle
$$
on the ordered input and target computational basis, where XOR is componentwise. The declared access contract states how many invocations count as queries and whether a controlled invocation is supplied. A query to this declared black box is counted separately from elementary gate size, depth, and width.

If $f$ is supplied instead by an explicit Boolean circuit, implementing $O_f$ means compiling that circuit and paying its reversible elementary-gate and workspace costs; the function description alone is not a free query. For this XOR oracle, its inverse is the same map, as proved in [[thm-qc-reversible-xor-oracle-unitary]]. Controlled access remains a separate capability unless the contract explicitly provides it.

Let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^m$ be total, let $s\in\{0,1\}^m$, and define the normalized character target
$$
|\chi_s\rangle=2^{-m/2}\sum_{y\in\{0,1\}^m}(-1)^{s\cdot y}|y\rangle,
$$
where $s\cdot y$ is the dot product modulo two. Then
$$
O_f(|x\rangle|\chi_s\rangle)=(-1)^{s\cdot f(x)}|x\rangle|\chi_s\rangle.
$$
For a one-bit output with $s=1$, $|\chi_s\rangle=|-\rangle=(|0\rangle-|1\rangle)/\sqrt2=H|1\rangle$. Thus the phase action is obtained with one invocation of the declared XOR oracle, with target preparation cost accounted separately.

Let $n,m\ge0$, $x\in\{0,1\}^n$, and $y\in\{0,1\}^m$. Let a finite topologically ordered Boolean DAG have $S$ non-input nodes, including constants, and $E$ input-port uses counted with multiplicity. Its gates are NOT, AND, OR, and constants, with fan-in at most two, and it has $m$ ordered output ports computing $f(x)$. Under the fixed elementary alphabet in [[def-qc-elementary-circuit-resources]], counting each occurrence of $X$, CNOT, and Toffoli as one gate and one serial layer, [[alg-qc-reversible-embedding]] returns a circuit on the ordered input, target, and work registers implementing
$$
|x,y,0^w\rangle\longmapsto|x,y\oplus f(x),0^w\rangle
$$
for every basis input $x$ and every target string $y$. It uses at most $6S+4E+m$ elementary gate occurrences, at most $S+E$ clean work bits, and serial depth at most $6S+4E+m$. The same operator action holds coherently on arbitrary superpositions and after adjoining any finite reference register.

For every total Boolean function $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}^m$, including noninjective functions, the coherent XOR oracle $O_f|x,y\rangle=|x,y\oplus f(x)\rangle$ is unitary and satisfies $O_f^2=I$. Hence $O_f^{-1}=O_f$.

Let $C=\mathbb C^2$ be a control qubit with ordered orthonormal basis $|0\rangle,|1\rangle$, let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space, and let $U:H\to H$ be unitary. On the control-first register $C\otimes H$, define

$$C(U):=\begin{pmatrix}I_H&0\\0&U\end{pmatrix}.$$

Thus $C(U)(|0\rangle\otimes v)=|0\rangle\otimes v$ and $C(U)(|1\rangle\otimes v)=|1\rangle\otimes Uv$. **Controlled access** means that the chosen operation model explicitly grants a call to this block operator. An ordinary call to a black-box $U$ does not silently grant a controlled call, and no query or gate cost is assigned unless the model states it.

Fix a finite gate alphabet $G$ with maximum arity $k:=\max(\{r(g):g\in G\}\cup\{0\})$ and a circuit from [[def-qc-circuit-syntax-and-register-order]]. The declared **size** is the number of gate occurrences, equivalently $\sum_{t=1}^d|L_t|$; the declared **depth** is the number $d$ of explicit layers, not a minimum over alternate layerings; the **width** is the number $n$ of all wires, including workspace wires. The operation model may also assign weighted gate costs, classical bit costs, and query costs; these are separate coordinates and are summed over the calls actually made.

A workspace wire is an ancilla. A **clean-ancilla promise** specifies computational-basis zero states for the ancillas and requires their exact return for every allowed data input: if $U$ is the implemented unitary, $V_D$ is the declared data unitary, and $|0_A\rangle$ is the specified joint zero vector, then $U(x\otimes|0_A\rangle)=V_Dx\otimes|0_A\rangle$ for every allowed data vector $x$. A **dirty-ancilla promise** permits an arbitrary ancilla state independent of the data input; it may be correlated with an untouched reference. Exact dirty-ancilla restoration means the implemented unitary on data and ancillas is $V_D\otimes I_A$ on the entire joint space, where $V_D$ is the declared unitary on data. The same operator equality then holds after tensoring with the identity on any finite untouched reference. Consequently, product input between the data and the combined ancilla/reference system remains product after the operation. No uncorrelated-output claim is made for an initially data-correlated ancilla.

A controlled or inverse operation is counted only when the operation model explicitly grants that access or supplies a construction; its charge is recorded separately from an ordinary call. Inverse availability and query or gate charges are also recorded separately from controlled forward access. In particular, the matrix of $U$ alone supplies neither a controlled call nor an inverse query, in accordance with [[def-qc-controlled-unitary-access]] and [[def-qc-inverse-unitary-access]].

derivations.claim: A phase oracle for a Boolean function $g$ means the diagonal map $P_g|x\rangle=(-1)^{g(x)}|x\rangle$, and a declared query contract counts each invocation of its named black box as one query. If the supplied black box is instead the XOR map, [F2] gives the same phase action using exactly one XOR-oracle invocation; target-state preparation is a separate ordinary circuit operation, charged in the separate coordinates of [F6].

If the only input for $f$ is an explicit Boolean circuit, [F3] replaces each required function evaluation by its finite compiled gate list, so the listed gates, depth, and work are charged under the separate resource coordinates [F6].
